candidate_seeds.name: Quirk (infracolor string) signatures at ATLAS/CMS: timing, ionisation, stopped-quirk and out-of-time annihilation
candidate_seeds.framework: Quirks / folded SUSY / quirky little Higgs / vector-like confinement with Lambda_IC << m_Q
candidate_seeds.idea: Heavy quarks charged under both SM and a confining hidden gauge group stay connected by a macroscopic string; pairs oscillate, lose energy in matter and annihilate late, giving non-standard tracks (bending, ionisation, out-of-time decays). Theory papers 2008-2018 proposed several strategies; the 2026 FASER result is the only LHC-experiment quirk search I found, none from ATLAS/CMS in my INSPIRE query.
candidate_seeds.signature_hypothesis: Highly ionising, non-helical tracks and out-of-time/delayed calorimeter or muon-system deposits from annihilating quirkonium; stopped-quirk decays in the empty-bunch window; delayed tracks in forward detectors.

gap_evidence.quote: We propose several simple modifications to the existing out-of-time search strategy that can give these searches sensitivity in regions of quirk parameter space not covered by any existing or proposed search strategy.

candidate_seeds.name: Dark Higgs-strahlung (h_D A') at the LHC
candidate_seeds.framework: Hidden Abelian Higgs model: dark photon + dark Higgs
candidate_seeds.idea: If a dark Higgs gives the dark photon mass, it is produced with the dark photon via Higgs-strahlung; B-factories searched it but the LHC white paper states no LHC search is sensitive.
candidate_seeds.signature_hypothesis: Prompt or displaced lepton-jet / dimuon pairs plus a boosted dark-Higgs decay (b-bbar or A'A' multi-lepton) in pp collisions; Z*->A' h_D at HL-LHC.

gap_evidence.quote: However, there are currently no searches at the LHC that are sensitive to this process.

candidate_seeds.name: Lifetime ~1 cm blind spot for H -> phi phi -> 4j (L1 track trigger / displaced jets)
candidate_seeds.framework: Exotic Higgs decays to long-lived scalars (hidden valley / Higgs portal)
candidate_seeds.idea: HL-LHC study states a blind spot around c*tau ~ 1 cm for Higgs decays to long-lived scalars; extending the L1 track trigger to larger impact parameters would give large gains, also for heavy SM-like Higgs bosons.
candidate_seeds.signature_hypothesis: Displaced multi-jet vertices with tracks of impact parameter few mm-cm, produced in ggF/VBF/VH with L1 track-trigger or HLT displaced-track selection.

gap_evidence.quote: In particular, there is cur- rently an blind spot for lifetimes of order 1 cm in searches for new long-lived scalars φ in Higgs decays, i.e. H(125) → φφ → 4j.
This is an important blind spot for searches, especially for the rare exotic Higgs boson decays like H → φφ.

candidate_seeds.notes: Projection exists (CMS-FTR-18-018 inside CERN-2019-007 addendum); whether Run-3 triggers closed the gap is not checked (UNVERIFIED).

candidate_seeds.name: Freeze-out LLPs with small mass splitting: soft displaced visible decays
candidate_seeds.framework: Long-lived particles from freeze-out/co-annihilation with compressed spectra
candidate_seeds.idea: Les Houches 2019 identifies blind spots across decay lengths 1 mm-1 m for LLPs with compressed mass splittings, whose displaced decays are soft and missed by displaced-jet/delayed-jet searches targeted at other benchmarks.
candidate_seeds.signature_hypothesis: Soft displaced vertices / displaced low-pT tracks recoiling against ISR jet or MET at HL-LHC with dedicated soft-track triggers.

gap_evidence.quote: We study various search strategies covering the whole range of possible decay lengths O(1 mm − 1 m), pointing out blind spots in the experimental search programme and estimating the corresponding potential for improvement.
Furthermore, displaced and delayed jets searches are not targeted to small mass splittings, and hence soft visible decays of the long-lived parent particle.

candidate_seeds.name: Mixed leptoquark final state b nu t tau (S1 with DM mediator / balanced BRs)
candidate_seeds.framework: S1 leptoquark with decays to t tau, b nu (and exotic channel)
candidate_seeds.idea: ATLAS searches assume BR(S1->b nu)=1-BR(S1->t tau), but for generic couplings both are ~50%, giving a mixed b nu t tau final state with no search; also single-LQ production with tau tau c has no search.
candidate_seeds.signature_hypothesis: Pair production with one t->b l nu... leg and one b + MET leg: b-jets, tau, MET with ttbar-like background; single-LQ tau tau c.

gap_evidence.quote: We note that even if this search is restricted to the third generation final states, there is no search for the “mixed" final state, namely bνtτ .
No search for this channel exists in the literature, but the CMS Collaboration has published a search for single leptoquark production in the τ τ b channel [23].

candidate_seeds.name: Top-quark couplings to Z/H with right-handed tops: Z t_R t_R and h Z t_R t_R
candidate_seeds.framework: Composite/top-partner EWSB: modified top electroweak couplings
candidate_seeds.idea: Les Houches: ZtRtR and hZtRtR couplings remain poorly constrained relative to light quarks. ttZ/ttH and tZq measurements constrain some combinations, but dedicated tt+Z/h kinematic observables for a single chirality are not what the standard analyses extract.
candidate_seeds.signature_hypothesis: ttZ, ttH, tZj, tttt differential distributions and polarisation observables sensitive to the right-handed top coupling.

gap_evidence.quote: For example, the ZtR t̄R and hZtR t̄R couplings, the focus of this chapter, are still poorly constrained compared to the analogous couplings to lighter quarks which were precisely measured by LEP in Z-boson decays.

candidate_seeds.name: High-charge (|z|>7) and fractionally charged particles beyond Drell-Yan: HL-LHC acceptance and trigger limits
candidate_seeds.framework: Multi-charged / fractionally charged / magnetic-charge-like exotic states
candidate_seeds.idea: ATLAS multi-charged search is limited to z<=7 because muon reconstruction fails above; FCPs are probed down to charge limits only for dE/dx tracks; production assumed Drell-Yan plus photon fusion only (spin, pair-vs-single assumptions).
candidate_seeds.signature_hypothesis: Heavily ionising tracks with dE/dx-based trigger (L1 timing window beta>0.65) and non-muon reconstruction for z>7.

gap_evidence.quote: The main reason for the search to be limited to a maximum of 𝑧 = 7 is that MCPs with higher charges will fail to be reconstructed as muons in at least 95% of cases.
This trigger is only sensitive to particles with velocity 𝛽 = 𝑣/𝑐 > 0.65 due to a timing window, within which particles must reach the MS, which limits the trigger efficiency.

candidate_seeds.idea: Top-partner pair production may be the primary discovery channel and possibly the only probe of sub-cm hidden-glueball decay lengths; relies on displaced-decay efficiencies not yet constructed.
